hero.subheadline: A funded seminar on the future of human rights in Ulaanbaatar
hero.valueProposition: Fully funded participation with airfare, accommodation, and meals for civil society, academic, and government delegates from Asia and Europe.

content.whyJoin:
The 24th Informal ASEM Seminar on Human Rights brings together civil society experts, academics, researchers, and government representatives from Asia and Europe for three days of dialogue in Ulaanbaatar. This year's theme, 'The Future of Human Rights - From Local to Global', turns ideas into practical steps through working groups focused on local, regional, and global protection.

Selected civil society participants attend for free, with hotel accommodation, meals, and economy-class airfare reimbursement covered. A two-day capacity-building training follows the seminar for interested participants, deepening the practical skills needed for follow-up action.

Because the seminar is co-organised by the Asia-Europe Foundation with Mongolia's National Human Rights Commission and Ministry of Foreign Affairs, it is a direct route into the Asia-Europe human rights policy community.
content.whoShouldApply:
This seminar is for human rights experts and practitioners from civil society organisations, NGOs, and academia, as well as people from relevant international, regional, or inter-governmental organisations and the private sector. You should apply if you are a citizen of an ASEM Partner country with working English proficiency and demonstrated knowledge of or interest in human rights, and you are willing to actively contribute to discussion and share the seminar's outcomes with your network.

Government representatives are nominated by their ASEM partner governments; everyone else applies through the open call.
benefits: Economy-class airfare reimbursement for civil society participants
Invitation to a two-day capacity-building training
Networking with human rights leaders from Asia and Europe
tips: Prepare an up-to-date CV and a motivational statement before you start the online form
Indicate your interest in the follow-on capacity-building programme in the same application form if you want to join it
Select your preferred working group level (global, regional, or local) thoughtfully
Submit before the deadline of 31 August 2026 at 23:59 Singapore time

shouldYouApply.idealFor: This is ideal for an established or early-career human rights professional, researcher, or civil society leader from an ASEM Partner country who wants a fully funded, high-level platform to exchange ideas and build a network across Asia and Europe.
goodFit: A professional working in a human rights NGO or civil society organisation
An academic or researcher on human rights issues
A representative of a national human rights institution
Someone keen to join the capacity-building training after the seminar
notIdealFor: Applicants who are not citizens of an ASEM Partner country
People without working proficiency in English
Anyone unable to attend the full programme in Ulaanbaatar in October 2026

faq.question: Who is eligible to apply?
faq.answer: Citizens of ASEM Partner countries from Asia and Europe with working English proficiency and knowledge of or interest in human rights. Civil society participants apply through the open call or are invited; government representatives are nominated by their governments.

faq.question: What costs are covered?
faq.answer: There is no registration or participation fee. Selected civil society participants receive accommodation, meals, and reimbursement of economy-class airfare up to a specified ceiling.

faq.question: Can I join the capacity-building training too?
faq.answer: Yes. The training runs on 15-16 October 2026 for selected seminar participants. Indicate your interest in the application form.

submissionGuide.detail: Apply through the official ASEF website, choosing whether you are applying for yourself or nominating someone else.
Provide your personal information and the details of your organisation.
Upload your up-to-date CV, motivational statement, and any other supporting documents in the participant profile section.
Choose your working group level (global, regional, or local) and indicate interest in the training programme if applicable.
Review the terms, check your information, and submit the form by 31 August 2026 at 23:59 Singapore time.
